      <title>College students rally in support of Starbucks baristas urging boycott over contract impasse</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/12/starbucks-workers-campus-rally-contract-talks</link>
      <description><p>Rallies will take place on more than US 40 campuses as workers seeking better pay and conditions decry stalled talks</p><p>Starbucks baristas, students, elected officials and allies are planning rallies at <a href="https://starbucksworkersunited.controlshift.app/events?link_id=2&amp;can_id=debd8d2ad19f005d15f9bbdff314d42a&amp;source=email-nov-12-day-of-action-for-starbucks-baristas&amp;email_referrer=email_3490793&amp;email_subject=nov-12-day-of-action-for-starbucks-baristas&amp;&amp;">over 40 college campuses</a> across the US on Thursday to support the Starbucks Workers United <a href="https://www.boycottstarbucks.net/">boycott campaign</a> as the union nears five years of deadlock with the company over contract negotiations.</p><p>Starbucks Workers United is <a href="https://sbworkersunited.org/what-were-fighting-for-updates-on-contract-bargaining/">seeking</a> better pay and stronger staffing levels, including a $17 an hour minimum wage for baristas and a minimum staffing of three workers per store. It has called on the public to <a href="https://www.boycottstarbucks.net/">boycott</a> Starbucks until its first contract is reached.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/12/starbucks-workers-campus-rally-contract-talks">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Home sales hit 16-year low in October amid record-high mortgage rates</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/12/home-sales-october-low</link>
      <description><p>Sales of built units fell to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, with mortgage rates at nearly three-year high</p><p>US existing home sales hit a 16-year low in October as buyers were driven away by record-high <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/money/mortgage-rates">mortgage rates</a> and rising inflation, according to new data released on Wednesday.</p><p>Sales of already built units dropped to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) reported. The median existing-home sales price increased slightly to $416,700. Declines in sales were seen in the midwest, south and west, though sales in the north-east held steady.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/12/home-sales-october-low">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Democrats’ US election sweep brings the price of their promised social contract into focus</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/11/democrats-election-medicaid-costs</link>
      <description><p>‘The post-election wish list is about to run into harsh fiscal reality: there is no money’</p><p>Is this an opportunity for a new America? As the Reagan revolution four decades ago launched US society down the path to low taxes and meager solidarity, perhaps the Republican bloodbath last week could turn US politics toward building a new social contract anchored on an aspiration to equitable prosperity.</p><p>One can sense the ambition of the bumper new crop of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/democrats">Democrats</a> ushered to power last week, calling for support for programs for children and their parents; emphatically endorsing the long-held dream of Medicare for All. The project includes rolling back <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s cuts to Medicaid and food stamps, and restoring subsidies for health insurance under the Affordable Care Act that Republicans allowed to expire. And that’s just the start.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/11/democrats-election-medicaid-costs">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Federal judge allows Trump’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/10/trump-10bn-defamation-lawsuit-bbc-allowed</link>
      <description><p>Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit</p><p>Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case. The president’s $10bn defamation lawsuit stems from the BBC’s splicing together of disparate comments he made before the 6 January US Capitol insurrection, as rendered in a Panorama documentary called Trump: A Second Chance.</p><p>“Accepting the allegations in the complaint as true, the Court finds Trump plausibly pled damages where Trump alleges a defamatory documentary released toward the election caused reputational harm,” the Trump-appointed Florida district court judge wrote. “It would be difficult for the Court to accept a different framing without completely negating the significance and fragility of political elections.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/10/trump-10bn-defamation-lawsuit-bbc-allowed">Continue reading...</a></description>
